pr_title: Don't assume that the `sleep` value is a dictionary in Tractive integration
pr_body:

## Breaking change
<!--

## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->
It seems that for some user accounts (or tracker models) the value of the `sleep` key is `null`, which causes a `TypeError`.

With this change we do not assume that the value of the `sleep` key is a dictionary. Additionally, `TypeError` catching has been added to eliminate similar problems in the future. There is no documentation for this API (reverse engineering), so we are not sure whether some tracker model returns `null` for another value used by the integration.

review_comments: I think you need to catch Exception if you want to capture similar problems in the future.
We don’t want to catch too broad exception.
Sure, but TypeError does not catch this problem. I don't know enough python, but maybe there is a better exception type to catch?

`TypeError` is exactly what we need here:
```
>>> None["lorem_ipsum"]
<stdin>:1: SyntaxWarning: 'NoneType' object is not subscriptable; perhaps you missed a comma?
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "<stdin>", line 1, in <module>
TypeError: 'NoneType' object is not subscriptable
```
Ah, ok. It was the `get('sleep', {}.get('...')` problem that TypeError didn't catch.
Yes, because of my mistake in the first fix you got `AttributeError`, this is why you had to catch `Exception` to make the code working.
It probably doesn't matter here but I'd probably use a local var for `event["sleep"]` so you don't have to do the lookup many times.
Good idea, I'm planning a small refactoring of Tractive and will follow your suggestion.
